title: Lilly Jumps on Raised Guidance, DoorDash Gains on Instacart Deal, Caterpillar and Sprouts Fall
dek: Earnings and deal news produced the biggest single-stock moves of the morning: Eli Lilly and Norwegian Cruise Line rose on beats, DoorDash climbed on its $17 billion Instacart deal, and Caterpillar and Sprouts Farmers Market fell.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: The Federal Reserve Building in Washington, D.C.

keyPoints: Eli Lilly rose about 8% after third-quarter revenue of $24.4 billion and EPS of $7.22, and raised 2026 revenue guidance to $91 billion-$92 billion from $85 billion-$87 billion (CNBC; Yahoo Finance).
DoorDash gained about 6% after agreeing to buy Instacart parent Maplebear for $17 billion in cash and stock; Instacart was down less than 1% (Investopedia).
Norwegian Cruise Line jumped about 13% after adjusted EPS of $1.12 beat the 93-cent consensus and revenue of $2.95 billion beat $2.88 billion (CNBC).

Caterpillar fell as much as 12% before trimming losses after a forecast of moderate fourth-quarter sales growth; Sprouts Farmers Market fell about 18% after cutting its profit outlook (Yahoo Finance).
body:
Eli Lilly was the morning's strongest large-cap mover. Shares rose about 8% on Thursday after the drugmaker reported third-quarter revenue of $24.4 billion, driven by Zepbound and Mounjaro, and raised its full-year revenue outlook to between $91 billion and $92 billion from $85 billion to $87 billion. Adjusted earnings were $7.22 a share, up from $6.21 a year earlier, according to CNBC's report of the release.

DoorDash shares gained about 6% after the company said it will buy food-delivery rival Instacart, parent of Maplebear, for $17 billion in cash and stock, per Investopedia. Instacart's shares were little changed, down less than 1%. The deal combines two of the largest U.S. grocery and restaurant delivery platforms.

Norwegian Cruise Line rose about 13% after reporting adjusted earnings of $1.12 per share against a FactSet consensus of 93 cents, and revenue of $2.95 billion against $2.88 billion expected, according to CNBC.

The losers were led by industrial and grocery names. Caterpillar fell as much as 12% in early trading before trimming losses; the company reported third-quarter adjusted EPS of $7.20 on revenue of $20.68 billion, slightly ahead of LSEG estimates, but forecast moderate fourth-quarter sales growth. Investopedia reported Caterpillar down nearly 8% at one point, and the drop weighed on the Dow. Sprouts Farmers Market fell about 18% after it cut its profit outlook and launched price cuts; JPMorgan's Thomas Palmer kept an overweight rating while calling the earnings reduction 'massive.'

Not every reaction was positive. ServiceNow plunged about 25% after its report, according to Investopedia, while Chipotle rose about 7% on same-store sales growth despite a slight EPS miss.

Investors will check whether the Lilly and DoorDash moves hold through the close; the figures above are as-of the times the cited outlets reported them.

The pattern across the morning is company-specific rather than macro-driven. Earnings and deal news, not the Fed or the GDP print, set the single-stock moves. Investors are weighing whether raised guidance at Lilly and a large acquisition at DoorDash can offset weaker outlooks at Caterpillar and Sprouts, and whether the AI-linked selloff in semiconductors and software extends beyond the open. CNBC, Investopedia and Yahoo Finance all reported these moves as early-session readings, so the levels can change materially before the close and should be checked against closing data.

marketImpact.summary: Company-specific news is doing most of the work this morning. Lilly's guidance raise and DoorDash's deal are the most market-relevant; Caterpillar's guide is a warning about AI-linked industrial demand.
marketImpact.timeframe: Thursday's session and the next earnings cycle

tickers.rationale: Shares up about 8% after Q3 revenue of $24.4 billion and a raised 2026 revenue outlook.
Up about 6% on the $17 billion cash-and-stock Instacart acquisition.
Fell as much as 12% after forecasting moderate Q4 sales growth despite a Q3 beat.
Down about 18% after a Q4 outlook far below consensus and a price-cutting plan.
